prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (max 500 words)

Overall approach
- Five missions: sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime and raise confidence in policing; break barriers to opportunity via childcare/education reform; build an NHS fit for the future. Mission-driven government, devolution of power, and long-term planning.

Fiscal and tax
- Fiscal rules: balance the current budget and have debt falling as a share of GDP by year five; OBR oversight of all major fiscal events.
- No rises in National Insurance, Income Tax rates (basic/higher/additional) or VAT.
- Tax measures: abolish non-dom status; close carried interest loophole; strengthen HMRC, reporting and enforcement against avoidance; end use of offshore trusts to avoid inheritance tax.

Economy and industry
- New Industrial Strategy and statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to leverage private investment: ports, gigafactories, steel decarbonisation, carbon capture, green hydrogen.
- Business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Ten-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for major projects, labs, datacentres; gigabit and 5G nationwide by 2030.
- SME support: tackle late payments; improve export help; reform British Business Bank; widen access to procurement.

Energy, climate, and nature
- Zero-carbon electricity by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine energy.
- Nuclear: extend existing plants; deliver Hinkley Point C, Sizewell C; support SMRs; maintain gas strategic reserve.
- No new oil and gas exploration licences; retain existing licences; ban fracking and new coal.
- Great British Energy (publicly owned) capitalised with £8.3bn; Local Power Plan; energy market regulation strengthened; reduce standing charges; upgrade grid.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum efficiency by 2030.
- Carbon border adjustment mechanism; transition plans mandated for major firms.
- Nature and water: new National River Walks, three National Forests, habitat expansion; stronger regulation and penalties for sewage pollution.
- Farming: 50% of public sector food local or higher standard; land-use framework; TB measures without badger cull.
- Animal welfare: bans on trail hunting, hunting trophy imports, puppy smuggling/farming, snares; work toward phasing out animal testing.

Health and social care
- 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week (evenings/weekends); shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; publish workforce plans.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation and clinical trials strategy; enhanced NHS app.
- Primary care: more GPs; face-to-face option; modern booking; pharmacist prescribing; direct referrals by opticians; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing.
- National Care Service framework with national standards, “home first,” discharge coordination; adult social care Fair Pay Agreement.
- Mental health: 8,500 additional staff; Young Futures hubs nationwide; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; youth vaping/energy drink restrictions; junk food ads to children banned.

Education, skills, and families
- 6,500 teachers in shortage subjects; reinstate School Support Staff Negotiating Body; leadership and regional improvement support; replace single Ofsted grade with report card; curriculum/assessment review; SEND inclusivity; school mental health support.
- 3,000 school-based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary.
- Skills England; guarantee for 18–21s (training/apprenticeship/support to work); reform Apprenticeship Levy into flexible Growth and Skills Levy; Technical Excellence Colleges; HE funding reform.
- Housing: 1.5m homes over the parliament; restore mandatory targets; more planners funded by higher non-UK buyer surcharge; brownfield first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; CPO reform; major boost to social/affordable housing; first-time buyer priority and permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Renters: abolish Section 21; empower challenges to unreasonable rent increases; extend Awaab’s Law; building safety and leasehold reforms (move to commonhold; ban new leasehold flats).

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; knife crime plan (mandatory intervention; ban certain blades; regulate online sales); Young Futures hubs; new child criminal exploitation offence.
- Specialist rape units in every force; specialist courts; domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms; stalking and spiking measures.
- Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; safeguards on child strip-searches; expanded fraud strategy; more detectives via direct entry.
- Prisons: expand capacity; reduce reoffending via education, pre-release plans, jobs; probation governance review.
- Historical injustices: Hillsborough Law; implement inquiry findings; Windrush Commissioner; review Orgreave.

Governance and devolution
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; stronger ministerial standards; restrict paid advisory/consultancy second jobs for MPs; Commons modernisation.
- Lords reform: end hereditary peers, retirement at 80, participation standards; longer-term replacement with a more representative second chamber.
- Voting: improve registration; fix voter ID inconsistencies; votes at 16; tighten donation rules.
- Reset relations with devolved governments; Council of the Nations and Regions; devolve powers/funding for growth and employment support.

Borders and immigration
- Border Security Command; counter-terror-style powers; EU security agreement; more caseworkers; end hotel use; returns unit (+1,000 staff) and new returns agreements.
- Reform points-based system; link migration to skills plans; workforce plans in key sectors; bar non-compliant employers from overseas recruitment.

Foreign, defence, and development
- NATO and nuclear deterrent commitments; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% GDP on defence; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for eligible non-UK veterans.
- Defence industrial strategy; procurement reform; support for Ukraine including asset repurposing.
- AUKUS commitment; China strategy audit; protect Overseas Territories.
- Trade: targeted FTAs and sector deals; WTO/CPTPP engagement; strategic partnerships incl. India and Gulf; support OECD global minimum tax.
- Clean Power Alliance internationally; restore development leadership in FCDO; aim to return to 0.7% ODA when fiscal conditions allow.
